title: HelpDeskPro — The Session That Was Already There
objective: Get a help-desk agent to end up authenticated under a session identifier you chose beforehand.

verifier.condition: A session identifier chosen before login (via the sid query parameter) is still the active, authenticated session identifier after a real login completes.

weakness: Login does not issue a fresh session identifier; if a session cookie is already present when a user logs in, the application simply upgrades the EXISTING session to authenticated, so an attacker who plants a known identifier on the victim beforehand inherits their authenticated session.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /?sid=<attacker-chosen value> then POST /login (session id unchanged across the login boundary)
seededData: Agent account alice with a known password. In-memory session store keyed by a plain session id.

credentials.label: Agent account
credentials.note: Sign in normally first and compare your session id before and after.

hints: Note your session cookie's value before you sign in, then check it again right after. Did it change?
This app accepts a ?sid= link to set your session id directly. What happens if you visit such a link, then sign in?
You don't need to steal anyone's session — you can hand them one of your own choosing.
burpNotes: Capture your session cookie before and after logging in via Repeater and compare the two raw values directly.
